newsitem.title: DENMARK: Positive Danish shares nudge up, more gains ahead.
newsitem.headline: Positive Danish shares nudge up, more gains ahead.

text.p: Danish share prices closed higher on Wednesday, bolstered by bond market rises and corporate news, with dealers seeing the gains continuing up to the weekend in a positive, pre-Yule trading atmosphere.
"Apart from bonds, which bucked up in the afternoon and corporate news, there is no reason for the rises. The KFX index could put on a quarter or half point tomorrow," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index gained 1.05 point to close at 131.15, while the KFX December future, due to expire on Friday, rose 0.60 point to 130.70 with 860 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.244 billion crowns.
In focus were notably ISS, Danisco and NKT. ISS ended two crowns down at 154 after climbing to 165 on the sale of its troubled U.S. ISS Inc unit to Canada's Aaxis.

Danisco, which posted first-half 1996/97 ordinary pre-tax profits eight percent up on last year and forecast a whole year profit 10-12 percent up on 1995/96, closed eight crowns up at 338. NKT finished a solid 20 crowns higher at 335 on a doubling of pre-tax profit expectations for whole year 1996 for its cable-making unit.
